topics.name: Filtering and sanitizing AI data, inputs, and outputs

requirements.title: Identifying security threats to the AI system
requirements.statement: AI-specific security threats to the deployed AI system are identified before new models are deployed, at least semiannually, and after AI-related security incidents, and are recorded in a threat register that describes each threat and the system components it affects.
requirements.note: Dual responsibility: the AI application provider and each AI service provider perform this independently.

elements.text: Threats identified before new models are deployed
Threats identified after AI-related security incidents
Threat register names the affected components (training data, models, APIs, etc.)

requirements.title: Threat modeling for the AI system
requirements.statement: Threat modeling evaluates the AI system's exposure to the identified threats, the countermeasures already in place, and the additional countermeasures needed given risk tolerance and the system's risk category; it is repeated when new threats are identified, before new models are deployed, at least semiannually, and after AI-related security incidents.
requirements.note: Dual responsibility.

elements.text: Threat modeling evaluates exposure to the identified threats
Threat modeling identifies countermeasures currently in place
Threat modeling identifies additional countermeasures needed, given risk tolerance and risk category
Performed when new threats are identified
Performed before new models are deployed

requirements.title: Security evaluations such as AI red teaming
requirements.statement: The AI system is security-assessed (e.g., AI red teaming, penetration testing) for AI-specific threats such as poisoning and model inversion before new models are deployed, before new or significantly changed supporting infrastructure is deployed, and at least annually, and risk treatment follows from the results.
requirements.note: Dual responsibility.

elements.text: Assessed before new models are deployed
Assessed before new or significantly modified supporting infrastructure is deployed
Risk treatment, including added countermeasures, taken based on results

requirements.title: Assign roles and responsibilities for AI
requirements.statement: Roles and responsibilities for governance, security, and risk management of the deployed AI system are formally defined (by extending an existing RACI or creating an AI-specific one), and human accountability for the system's actions, outputs, and decisions is formally assigned.
requirements.note: Dual responsibility.

elements.text: Roles defined for AI risk management
Human accountability formally assigned for AI actions, outputs, and decisions

requirements.title: Augment written policies to address AI specificities
requirements.statement: Where appropriate to the deployment context, written policies explicitly cover the organization's AI systems and their AI-specific characteristics across security administration, data governance, software development, risk management, incident management, business continuity, and disaster recovery.
requirements.note: Dual responsibility: the AI application provider and its AI service providers each perform this.

elements.text: Security administration policy covers AI systems
Data governance policy covers AI systems
Software development policy covers AI systems
Risk management policy covers AI systems
Incident management policy covers AI systems
Business continuity policy covers AI systems
Disaster recovery policy covers AI systems

requirements.title: Humans can intervene if needed
requirements.statement: The AI application lets human operators evaluate model outputs before relying on them and intervene in model-initiated actions (e.g., sending email, modifying records) when needed.
requirements.note: AI application provider's sole responsibility. Addresses confabulation and excessive agency.

elements.text: Operators can evaluate model outputs before relying on them
Operators can intervene in model-initiated actions when needed

requirements.title: Provide AI security training to AI builders and deployers
requirements.control_ref: 02.e Information Security Awareness, Education, and Training
requirements.statement: At least annually, AI security training (vulnerabilities, threats, policy requirements and similar topics) is provided to all teams that build and deploy AI software and models, including development, data science, and cybersecurity personnel.
requirements.note: Inheritance not confirmed from the public spec; treat as the organization's own responsibility unless MyCSF says otherwise.

elements.text: Annual AI security training for development personnel
Annual AI security training for data science personnel
Annual AI security training for cybersecurity personnel

requirements.title: Version control of AI assets
requirements.control_ref: 10.j Access Control to Program Source Code
requirements.statement: AI assets are versioned and tracked: model-creation code, training and fine-tuning datasets, RAG datasets, pipeline configurations, language model tool code, and models.
requirements.note: Fully inheritable; may be the AI platform provider's and/or model creator's sole responsibility.

elements.text: Code used to create, train, and/or deploy models

requirements.title: Inspection of AI software assets
requirements.statement: Downloaded models, software packages, and language model tools are inspected for exploitable vulnerabilities before use, and the organization acts on the results.
requirements.note: Fully inheritable.

elements.text: Downloaded software packages inspected before use
Language model tools inspected before use

requirements.title: Change control over AI models
requirements.statement: Model changes, including version upgrades and model replacements, are documented, tested, and approved under the software change control policy before deployment, and release notes are obtained and reviewed for upgrades to externally developed models.
requirements.note: Partially inheritable (AI application provider and AI platform provider). Can be N/A if no new models or versions were deployed in the past 12 months.

elements.text: Release notes obtained and reviewed for upgrades to externally developed models

requirements.title: Change control over language model tools
requirements.applies_text: generative only, only when agents/plugins/language model tools used
requirements.statement: Changes to agents and plugins are documented, tested, and approved under the software change control policy before deployment.
requirements.note: Generative AI only; applies only when agents or plugins are used. AI application provider's sole responsibility.

elements.text: Changes to agents/plugins approved before deployment

requirements.title: Documentation of AI specifics during system design and development
requirements.statement: System documentation covers the creation, operation, and lifecycle management of models, datasets, configurations, and language model tools, and the tooling, computing, and human resources the system needs.
requirements.note: Partially inheritable.

elements.text: Documentation covers system and computing resources

requirements.title: Linkage between dataset, model, and pipeline configuration
requirements.statement: When creating machine learning models, the link between training dataset versions, pipeline configuration, and the resulting model is explicitly documented.
requirements.note: ML models only. Fully inheritable; may be the AI model creator's sole responsibility (inherit when the client only consumes third-party models).

elements.text: Dataset version, pipeline configuration, and resulting model linkage documented

requirements.title: Verification of origin and integrity of AI assets
requirements.statement: Before use, cryptographic hashes and/or digital signatures are verified on downloaded models, software packages, datasets, and language model tools.
requirements.note: Fully inheritable (AI platform provider and/or model creator).

elements.text: Hash/signature verified on downloaded software packages
Hash/signature verified on language model tools

requirements.title: Identify and evaluate compliance and legal obligations for AI development and deployment
requirements.statement: Before deployment and at least annually, the organization assesses its compliance with legal and regulatory requirements for AI development and deployment, including liability for harmful outputs.
requirements.note: Dual responsibility.

elements.text: Compliance with applicable AI laws and regulations (including liability for outputs) assessed

requirements.title: Identify and evaluate constraints on data used for AI
requirements.statement: The organization assesses compliance with constraints on data used for training, validation, tuning, and RAG (laws, regulations, contracts, internal data governance, copyright and commercial interests), acts on the results, and does so before the data is used and at least annually.
requirements.note: ML models only. Dual responsibility.

elements.text: Assessed before the data is used for AI

requirements.title: Due diligence review of AI providers
requirements.control_ref: 09.f Monitoring and Review of Third Party Services
requirements.statement: The security posture of external commercial providers of AI models, datasets, software packages, platforms and infrastructure, and language model tools is evaluated at onboarding and routinely afterward.
requirements.note: Dual responsibility.

requirements.title: Review the model card of models used by the AI system
requirements.control_ref: 05.i Identification of Risks Related to External Parties
requirements.applies_text: all model types, only when externally sourced models used
requirements.statement: For externally sourced models deployed in production applications, the model card is reviewed before deployment.
requirements.note: Applies to externally sourced models in production. AI application provider's sole responsibility.

requirements.title: AI security requirements communicated to AI providers
requirements.control_ref: 05.k Addressing Security in Third Party Agreements
requirements.statement: Agreements with external providers of AI system components and services clearly communicate the organization's AI security requirements.
requirements.note: Joint responsibility, normally through a jointly executed agreement.

elements.text: Agreements with platform and infrastructure providers
Agreements with language model tool providers
Agreements for contracted AI system services

requirements.title: Data minimization or anonymization
requirements.applies_text: ML models (predictive, generative), Q2 yes (sensitive data used to train/tune/RAG)
requirements.statement: Data used for training, fine-tuning, and RAG prompt enhancement is reviewed to find fields or records that can be removed or anonymized to prevent leakage, and findings are acted on.
requirements.note: Only when confidential or sensitive data was used to train, tune, or enhance prompts (tailoring Q2). Not for rule-based-only systems. Fully inheritable.

requirements.title: Limit output specificity and precision
requirements.applies_text: ML models (predictive, generative), Q2 or Q3 yes
requirements.statement: The precision and specificity of AI outputs are reduced to limit an adversary's ability to extract information from the model or optimize attacks.
requirements.note: Only when sensitive data was used (Q2) or the model architecture is confidential (Q3). AI application provider's sole responsibility.

elements.text: Output precision reduced (e.g., rounded confidence values)
Output specificity reduced (e.g., coarser class labels)

requirements.title: Additional training data measures
requirements.statement: The organization evaluates whether additional training-data measures (e.g., adversarial training) are needed to make its ML models resistant to evasion and poisoning, documents the evaluation, repeats it at least semiannually and after AI security incidents, and implements the measures deemed necessary.
requirements.note: Non-generative (predictive) ML only. Fully inheritable (AI model creator).

elements.text: Evaluation revisited after AI-related security incidents

requirements.title: Limit the release of technical information about the AI system
requirements.applies_text: ML models (predictive, generative), Q3 yes (confidential model architecture)
requirements.statement: The release of technical AI project details is limited: architecture, datasets, algorithms, language model tools, safety and security checkpoints, and team information.
requirements.note: Only when model architectures are confidential to the organization (Q3). Dual responsibility.

elements.text: Training/testing/validation/tuning datasets of confidential or closed-source models
Algorithms of confidential or closed-source models
Architecture of confidential or closed-source models
Teams that develop and support the system

requirements.title: Model rate limiting / throttling
requirements.statement: The total number and the rate of API calls a user can make to the AI model over a period are limited, to resist denial of service and hinder attack experimentation.
requirements.note: Partially inheritable (AI application and AI platform providers).

elements.text: Total API calls per user per period limited
Rate of API calls per user limited

requirements.title: GenAI model least privilege
requirements.statement: The data and capabilities granted to generative models, including through agents and plugins, are restricted to least privilege and governed by the access management and authentication policies.
requirements.note: Generative AI only. AI application provider's sole responsibility.

elements.text: Generative model data access least privilege (incl. via agents/plugins)
Generative model capabilities least privilege (incl. via agents/plugins)
Access governed by access management policy (approvals, revocations, reviews)

requirements.title: Restrict access to data used for AI
requirements.statement: Access to training, testing, validation, fine-tuning, and RAG data (original and embedded) is restricted to least privilege under the access management policy and MFA-level authentication.
requirements.note: ML models only. Fully inheritable; may be the model creator's sole responsibility.

elements.text: Original (non-vectorized) RAG data access least privilege
Access governed by access management policy
Access governed by authentication policy (MFA or equivalent)

requirements.title: Restrict access to AI models
requirements.statement: The ability to access and modify deployed AI models is restricted to least privilege under the access management policy and MFA-level authentication.
requirements.note: ML models only. Fully inheritable; may be the AI platform provider's sole responsibility.

elements.text: Access to and modification of deployed models least privilege
Access governed by access management policy
Access governed by authentication policy (MFA or equivalent)

requirements.title: Restrict access to interact with the AI model
requirements.statement: The ability to interact with the production model through APIs, the AI application, and agents/plugins is restricted to least privilege under the access management and authentication policies.
requirements.note: Partially inheritable.

elements.text: Interaction via the AI application least privilege
Access governed by access management policy

requirements.title: Restrict access to the AI engineering environment and AI code
requirements.statement: Access to AI engineering environments, code that creates, trains, or deploys models, and agent/plugin code is restricted to least privilege under the access management policy and MFA-level authentication.
requirements.note: Partially inheritable.

elements.text: AI engineering environment access least privilege
Model create/train/deploy code access least privilege
Access governed by access management policy
Access governed by authentication policy (MFA or equivalent)

requirements.title: Encrypt traffic to and from the AI model
requirements.statement: Communication channels between the model and the interface that displays its outputs are encrypted with secure protocols such as TLS.
requirements.note: Fully inheritable; may be the AI application provider's sole responsibility.

elements.text: Model-to-interface channels encrypted with secure protocols

requirements.title: Encrypt AI assets at rest
requirements.applies_text: ML models (predictive, generative), Q2 or Q3 yes
requirements.statement: Training, testing, validation and fine-tuning datasets, embeddings, and models are encrypted at rest in line with the organization's encryption strength and key management policies.
requirements.note: Only when sensitive data was used (Q2) or the architecture is confidential (Q3). Fully inheritable.

requirements.title: Log AI system inputs and outputs
requirements.statement: Every model input and output is logged with the exact content, timestamp, requesting account, request origin, and model version, and the logs are retained, protected, and sanitized under policy.
requirements.note: Partially inheritable.

elements.text: Date and time of input logged
Logs retained, protected, and sanitized per policy

requirements.title: Monitor AI system inputs and outputs
requirements.statement: At least monthly, model inputs and outputs are monitored for signs of attack or compromise, and filters and guardrails are confirmed to work as intended.
requirements.note: Partially inheritable.

elements.text: Inputs monitored at least monthly and input filters confirmed working
Outputs monitored at least monthly and output filters confirmed working

requirements.title: Monitoring data, models, and configurations for suspicious changes
requirements.statement: At least monthly, AI datasets, models, AI-relevant code (including agent and plugin code), and AI configurations such as metaprompts are checked for suspicious manipulation.
requirements.note: Partially inheritable.

elements.text: AI datasets monitored monthly for manipulation
AI models monitored monthly for manipulation
AI-relevant code monitored monthly for manipulation
AI configurations (e.g., metaprompts) monitored monthly for manipulation

requirements.title: Inventory deployed AI systems
requirements.statement: A documented inventory of deployed AI systems lists AI platforms, model names and versions, system owner, sensitivity/risk categorization, and AI service providers, and is reviewed and updated at least semiannually.
requirements.note: Dual responsibility. The spec's statement says semiannual; its illustrative procedure says annual. Assess to semiannual.

elements.text: Inventory lists models with name and version
Inventory lists sensitivity or risk categorization
Inventory reviewed and updated at least semiannually

requirements.title: Maintain a catalog of trusted data sources for AI
requirements.statement: A catalog of trusted data sources for training, testing, validation, fine-tuning, and RAG prompt enhancement is maintained and reviewed at least semiannually.
requirements.note: ML models only. Fully inheritable; may be the model creator's sole responsibility.

elements.text: Trusted sources cataloged for training/testing/validation data
Trusted sources cataloged for fine-tuning data
Trusted sources cataloged for RAG data
Catalog reviewed and updated at least semiannually

requirements.title: AI data and data supply inventory
requirements.statement: A documented inventory of data used for training, testing, validation, fine-tuning, and RAG records each source's provenance and sensitivity level and is reviewed at least semiannually.
requirements.note: ML models only. Fully inheritable.

elements.text: Inventory reviewed and updated at least semiannually

requirements.title: Model card publication (for model builders)
requirements.applies_text: ML models (predictive, generative), only when the organization builds models
requirements.statement: Model builders publish a model card for each model they produce, covering model details, intended use, training details, evaluation details, and caveats and recommendations.
requirements.note: ML models only; applies only to organizations that build models.

elements.text: Model card includes caveats and recommendations

requirements.topic: Filtering and sanitizing AI data, inputs, and outputs
requirements.title: Dataset sanitization
requirements.statement: Data used for training, fine-tuning, and RAG is checked before use for suspicious or adversarial patterns such as poisoned samples, and anomalous entries are removed.
requirements.note: ML models only. Fully inheritable.

requirements.topic: Filtering and sanitizing AI data, inputs, and outputs
requirements.title: Input filtering
requirements.statement: Before inputs reach the model, user inputs of any modality or source (including attachments) are actively filtered for suspicious or unexpected values or patterns that could be adversarial.
requirements.note: Partially inheritable (AI platform provider, if used, and AI application provider).

elements.text: User inputs filtered for suspicious or unexpected patterns before model processing

requirements.topic: Filtering and sanitizing AI data, inputs, and outputs
requirements.title: Output encoding
requirements.statement: Textual model output is encoded to prevent traditional injection attacks such as remote code execution.
requirements.note: Generative AI only. Partially inheritable.

elements.text: Output encoding applied to textual model output

requirements.topic: Filtering and sanitizing AI data, inputs, and outputs
requirements.title: Output filtering
requirements.statement: Unless specifically required otherwise, sensitive data (e.g., personal phone numbers) in generative model output is filtered or prevented from reaching end users.
requirements.note: Generative AI only. Partially inheritable.

elements.text: Sensitive data filtered or prevented in generative output

requirements.title: Updating incident response for AI specifics
requirements.statement: Incident detection and response addresses AI-specific threats (e.g., poisoning, evasion) through updated plans and playbooks, AI-focused tabletop exercises, recorded AI incidents, and logs and alerts from deployed AI systems feeding monitoring and detection tools.
requirements.note: Dual responsibility.

elements.text: Incident plans/playbooks updated for AI-specific threats
AI-specific threats included in tabletop exercises
Specifics of AI security incidents recorded
AI system logs feed monitoring/detection tools
AI system alerts feed monitoring/detection tools

requirements.title: Backing up AI system assets
requirements.statement: Backups are made of AI training, test and validation data, model creation and deployment code, fine-tuning data, models, language model tools, AI configurations, and RAG data, and are managed under the backup policies.
requirements.note: Partially inheritable.

elements.text: Backups managed under data and software backup policies
